theme: 3 terms on popups: the object that shows them, the buttons inside, and the menu that slides up

terms.definition: An object that shows a popup message with a title and buttons.
terms.example: Show an Alert Controller when the upload fails.
terms.code:
let alert = UIAlertController(
    title: "Upload failed",
    message: "Try again later.",
    preferredStyle: .alert)

terms.definition: A button in an alert, with a title, a style and the code to run when it's tapped.
terms.example: Make Delete a destructive Alert Action, so it turns red.

terms.definition: A menu of choices that slides up from the bottom, instead of a centered popup.
terms.example: Use an Action Sheet for share options, not an alert.

quizzes.question: What do you call a menu of choices that slides up from the bottom?
What is a button inside an alert, with a title, a style and code to run?
In this code, what object shows the popup message?
quizzes.code:
let alert = UIAlertController(
    title: "Oops", message: nil,
    preferredStyle: .alert)
present(alert, animated: true)

video.description:
Learn to explain how alerts and action sheets are built: Alert Controller, Alert Action & Action Sheet, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Alert Controller - An object that shows a popup message with a title and buttons.
Alert Action - A button in an alert, with a title, a style and the code to run when it's tapped.
Action Sheet - A menu of choices that slides up from the bottom, instead of a centered popup.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

dialogue.title: The delete popup crashes on iPad

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the delete confirmation crashes on iPad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is it an Alert Controller with the action sheet style?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, like in the code. It works on iPhone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On iPad, an Action Sheet appears as a popover, so it needs a source view.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ah. I never set the source.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Set a source view for the popover, or switch to the alert style.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Which one fits a delete confirmation?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An alert is simple. An Action Sheet is better for many choices.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the Delete button is an Alert Action, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Make it a destructive Alert Action, so it turns red.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. I'll use the alert style for this one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. The same Alert Controller supports both styles.

dialogue.code:
let alert = UIAlertController(
    title: "Delete note?", message: nil,
    preferredStyle: .actionSheet)
alert.addAction(UIAlertAction(title: "Delete",
    style: .destructive))
present(alert, animated: true)
